svg.content: <mxfile host="app.diagrams.net" scale="1" border="0"> <diagram name="OAuth2 Architecture" id="MSfRcxjyI9uDXzvHbdzS"> <mxGraphModel dx="1187" dy="867" grid="1" gridSize="10" guides="1" tooltips="1" connect="1" arrows="1" fold="1" page="1" pageScale="1" pageWidth="850" pageHeight="1100" math="0" shadow="0"> <root> <mxCell id="0" /> <mxCell id="1" parent="0" /> <mxCell id="vrJ4jLp43krrCrDhC420-1" parent="1" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;align=left;verticalAlign=top;fontSize=24;fontColor=#222222;fontStyle=1;spacing=4;" value="OAuth 2.0 — Architecture &amp; Decisions" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="36" width="1700" x="40" y="8" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="vrJ4jLp43krrCrDhC420-2" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=13;fillColor=#f8cecc;strokeColor=#b85450;strokeWidth=1.5;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Goal:</b> let an app act for a user with LIMITED, TEMPORARY, REVOCABLE access — without ever seeing the user's password &nbsp;|&nbsp; <b>Rule:</b> never put a long-lived secret where an attacker can read it (URL, browser storage, logs) &nbsp;|&nbsp; <b>Remember:</b> OAuth 2 = authorization (what you may do); OIDC adds authentication (who you are)" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="44" width="1880" x="40" y="48" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="vrJ4jLp43krrCrDhC420-3" parent="1" style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=none;dashed=1;dashPattern=8 4;strokeColor=#b26a00;verticalAlign=top;align=left;spacingLeft=12;spacingTop=4;fontStyle=1;fontSize=14;fontColor=#b26a00;" value="A · WHY OAUTH, AND WHICH GRANT?" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="190" width="1910" x="20" y="100" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="vrJ4jLp43krrCrDhC420-4" parent="1" style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=none;dashed=1;dashPattern=8 4;strokeColor=#1a56a0;verticalAlign=top;align=left;spacingLeft=12;spacingTop=4;fontStyle=1;fontSize=14;fontColor=#1a56a0;" value="B · THE FLOW — Authorization Code + PKCE (a user is present)" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="370" width="1910" x="20" y="310" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="vrJ4jLp43krrCrDhC420-5" parent="1" style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=none;dashed=1;dashPattern=8 4;strokeColor=#9673a6;verticalAlign=top;align=left;spacingLeft=12;spacingTop=4;fontStyle=1;fontSize=14;fontColor=#9673a6;" value="C · INSIDE THE SYSTEM — components, and how they stay safe and alive" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="545" width="1910" x="20" y="700" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="vrJ4jLp43krrCrDhC420-6" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=11;fillColor=#f8cecc;strokeColor=#b85450;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Problem:</b> a budgeting app wants to read your mutual-fund holdings. Giving it your PASSWORD means full access, forever, and you cannot cut off just that one app." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="130" width="430" x="40" y="140" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="vrJ4jLp43krrCrDhC420-7" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=12;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#82b366;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Decision:</b> give the app a TOKEN instead — limited (scopes), temporary (expiry), revocable." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="130" width="430" x="520" y="140" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="vrJ4jLp43krrCrDhC420-8" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=11;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Which grant?</b><br>User present (web / mobile / SPA) → <b>Auth Code + PKCE</b><br>No user (service → service) → <b>Client Credentials</b><br>No browser (TV / CLI) → <b>Device Code</b>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="130" width="430" x="1000" y="140" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="vrJ4jLp43krrCrDhC420-9" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=11;fillColor=#f5f5f5;strokeColor=#666666;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Rejected:</b> Implicit grant (token sits in the URL) and Password grant (password handed to the app). Both are deprecated for good reason." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="130" width="430" x="1480" y="140" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="vrJ4jLp43krrCrDhC420-10" edge="1" parent="1" value="<b>Client app</b><br>makes a PKCE secret + state, then sends the user's browser to the Authorization Server" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="105" width="275" x="40" y="385" as="geometry" /> value="<b>Authorization Server</b><br>checks client + redirect URI, user logs in (MFA) and approves the scopes" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="105" width="275" x="355" y="385" as="geometry" /> value="<b>Authorization code</b><br>returned through the browser redirect — short-lived, single-use" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="105" width="275" x="670" y="385" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell value="<b>Token exchange</b><br>client sends code + PKCE verifier (+ its own credentials) to /token" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="105" width="275" x="985" y="385" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell value="<b>Tokens issued</b><br>access token (minutes) + refresh token (rotating)" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="105" width="275" x="1300" y="385" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell target="vrJ4jLp43krrCrDhC420-21" value="⑤"> <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="vrJ4jLp43krrCrDhC420-27" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Q: Why PKCE?</b> Mobile apps and SPAs cannot keep a secret. A one-time challenge/verifier pair makes a stolen code useless. <i>Cost:</i> a few lines of client code. Always use it." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="150" width="275" x="40" y="505" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="vrJ4jLp43krrCrDhC420-28" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Q: How do we stop forged callbacks and code theft?</b> Exact-match redirect_uri list + a state check (anti-CSRF) + least-privilege scopes. <i>Trade-off:</i> no wildcards and fine scopes mean more registration and consent friction." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="150" width="275" x="355" y="505" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="vrJ4jLp43krrCrDhC420-29" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Q: Why return a code, not the token?</b> Browser URLs leak (history, logs, referrer). The code lives ~60 s, works once, and is useless without the verifier." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="150" width="275" x="670" y="505" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="vrJ4jLp43krrCrDhC420-30" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Q: Why a separate back channel?</b> Tokens travel server-to-server, never through the browser. Confidential clients prove identity (secret / private-key JWT / mTLS); public clients rely on PKCE." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="150" width="275" x="985" y="505" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="vrJ4jLp43krrCrDhC420-31" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Q: How long should tokens live?</b> Short access, longer refresh. <i>Trade-off:</i> shorter = safer but more traffic to the AS; longer = fewer calls but a bigger blast radius if stolen." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="150" width="275" x="1300" y="505" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="vrJ4jLp43krrCrDhC420-32" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Q: Where does the client keep tokens?</b> In a backend / BFF or httpOnly cookie, not localStorage — XSS can read browser storage. <i>Cost:</i> a BFF is one more component to run." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="150" width="275" x="1615" y="505" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="vrJ4jLp43krrCrDhC420-33" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=11;fillColor=#dae8fc;strokeColor=#6c8ebf;strokeWidth=1.5;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Client app</b><br>confidential: backend / BFF (can hold a secret)<br>public: mobile / SPA (cannot — uses PKCE)" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="190" width="230" x="40" y="790" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="vrJ4jLp43krrCrDhC420-34" parent="1" value="<b>Code &amp; token store</b><br>fast, TTL, one-time use" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="90" width="225" x="1095" y="795" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="vrJ4jLp43krrCrDhC420-39" id="vrJ4jLp43krrCrDhC420-40" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=11;fillColor=#ffffff;strokeColor=#999999;strokeWidth=1.5;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Refresh families + revocation</b><br>rotate on use · revoke on reuse or logout" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="90" width="300" x="680" y="900" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=11;fillColor=#ffffff;strokeColor=#999999;strokeWidth=1.5;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Rate limit + audit log</b><br>protect /token and login · record every grant" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="90" width="320" x="1000" y="900" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="vrJ4jLp43krrCrDhC420-42" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=11;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#82b366;strokeWidth=1.5;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Resource server / API gateway</b><br>validates the token on every call: JWT checked locally with cached public keys, or opaque token checked by asking the AS (introspection). Then checks the scope." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="190" width="490" x="1400" y="790" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="vrJ4jLp43krrCrDhC420-43" edge="1" parent="1" source="vrJ4jLp43krrCrDhC420-33" style="edgeStyle=orthogonalEdgeStyle;rounded=1;html=1;endArrow=block;endFill=1;strokeWidth=2;strokeColor=#1a56a0;fontSize=11;fontColor=#1a56a0;labelBackgroundColor=#ffffff;fontSize=15;fontStyle=1;" target="vrJ4jLp43krrCrDhC420-34" value="⑥ refresh / token calls"> <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="vrJ4jLp43krrCrDhC420-44" edge="1" parent="1" source="vrJ4jLp43krrCrDhC420-42" style="edgeStyle=orthogonalEdgeStyle;rounded=1;html=1;endArrow=block;endFill=1;strokeWidth=2;strokeColor=#d79b00;fontSize=11;fontColor=#d79b00;labelBackgroundColor=#ffffff;dashed=1;fontSize=15;fontStyle=1;exitX=0.5;exitY=1;entryX=0.5;entryY=1;" target="vrJ4jLp43krrCrDhC420-39" value="⑦ fetch + cache public keys"> <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry"> <Array as="points"> <mxPoint x="1645" y="1045" /> <mxPoint x="510" y="1045" /> </Array> </mxGeometry> </mxCell> <mxCell id="vrJ4jLp43krrCrDhC420-45" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Q: JWT or opaque access tokens?</b> JWT = self-contained, the API validates locally (AS stays off the hot path) but it cannot be revoked until it expires. Opaque = revoke instantly, but every API call asks the AS. <i>Our pick:</i> short JWT (5–15 min) + opaque rotating refresh; introspect only for high-risk actions like payments." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="150" width="420" x="40" y="1075" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="vrJ4jLp43krrCrDhC420-46" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Q: What if a refresh token is stolen?</b> Rotate it on every use; if an OLD one is replayed, revoke the whole token family. <i>Trade-off:</i> the AS must now store refresh state, and a flaky network can cause a false lock-out." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="150" width="420" x="510" y="1075" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="vrJ4jLp43krrCrDhC420-47" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Q: How can an API verify tokens without a shared secret?</b> The AS signs with a private key (RS256 / ES256); APIs fetch public keys from JWKS and cache them; keys rotate by kid. <i>Why not HS256:</i> a shared secret lets every API forge tokens." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="150" width="420" x="980" y="1075" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="vrJ4jLp43krrCrDhC420-48" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Q: What if the AS is down or attacked?</b> Stateless AS behind a load balancer; codes in a fast store (single-use, ~60 s); rate-limit /token and login. Valid JWTs keep working until expiry; new logins fail. <i>Trade-off:</i> longer JWT life = more outage tolerance, slower revocation." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="150" width="420" x="1450" y="1075" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="vrJ4jLp43krrCrDhC420-49" parent="1" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;align=left;verticalAlign=top;fontSize=16;fontColor=#222222;fontStyle=1;spacing=4;" value="How to read it — follow the numbers" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="30" width="900" x="40" y="1270" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="vrJ4jLp43krrCrDhC420-50" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=12;fillColor=#ffffff;strokeColor=#999999;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Flow (①–⑦)</b><br>① The client sends the user's browser to the Authorization Server, with a PKCE challenge and a state value.<br>② The user logs in and approves only the scopes asked for; the AS issues a one-time code.<br>③ The browser carries the code back to the client.<br>④ The client swaps code + PKCE verifier for tokens, directly with the AS (back channel).<br>⑤ The client calls the API with the access token.<br>⑥ When the access token expires, the client uses the refresh token to get a new pair.<br>⑦ APIs fetch and cache the AS's public keys to verify tokens locally.<br><br><b>Example:</b> a budgeting app wants your holdings. You log in at the bank's Authorization Server, approve only "holdings.read", and the app gets a 10-minute token. The portfolio API checks that scope — and nothing else works with it." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="490" width="610" x="40" y="1310" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="vrJ4jLp43krrCrDhC420-51" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=12;fillColor=#ffffff;strokeColor=#999999;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Architect decisions — say "why A over B"</b><br>1. Tokens over passwords: limited, temporary, revocable.<br>2. Auth Code + PKCE over Implicit / Password: nothing sensitive travels in a URL.<br>3. Front channel for the user, back channel for secrets.<br>4. Exact redirect_uri + state: stops code theft and CSRF.<br>5. Least-privilege scopes: a small blast radius if a token leaks.<br>6. Short access + rotating refresh: balance safety, user experience and AS load.<br>7. JWT vs opaque: speed vs instant revocation — choose by risk.<br>8. Asymmetric keys + JWKS: APIs can verify without being able to forge.<br>9. Tokens in a backend / BFF, never localStorage.<br>10. Client Credentials for machines: no user, no consent screen.<br>11. OAuth 2 says what you may do; add OIDC (ID token) to know who you are." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="490" width="610" x="670" y="1310" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="vrJ4jLp43krrCrDhC420-52" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=12;fillColor=#ffffff;strokeColor=#999999;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Mental model &amp; interview close</b><br><i>Delegate → Authenticate → Consent → Code → Exchange → Token → Validate → Refresh → Revoke</i><br><br><b>Trade-offs we accept</b><br>• PKCE + BFF → extra client work and one more component<br>• Short tokens → more refresh traffic on the AS<br>• Refresh rotation → the AS keeps state; rare false lock-outs<br>• JWT → slower revocation (until expiry)<br>• Strict redirect URIs → more registration work<br>• Fine-grained scopes → more consent friction<br><br><b>One-line close:</b> "OAuth 2 lets an app act for a user without ever holding their password — safe because every secret travels on the channel an attacker cannot read, and every token is small, short-lived and checkable."<br><br><b>Honest test:</b> an access token leaks into a log file — how much damage, for how long? It should be one API area, for a few minutes. That is the design working." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="490" width="630" x="1300" y="1310" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> </root> </mxGraphModel> </diagram> </mxfile>

div.div: OAuth 2.0 — Architecture & Decisions

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(248, 206, 204), rgb(81, 45, 43)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(184, 84, 80), rgb(215, 129, 126));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 1862px; height: 1px; padding-top: 62px; margin-left: 29px;

div.div: Goal: let an app act for a user with LIMITED, TEMPORARY, REVOCABLE access — without ever seeing the user's password | Rule: never put a long-lived secret where an attacker can read it (URL, browser storage, logs) | Remember: OAuth 2 = authorization (what you may do); OIDC adds authentication (who you are)

div.div: C · INSIDE THE SYSTEM — components, and how they stay safe and alive

div.div: Problem: a budgeting app wants to read your mutual-fund holdings. Giving it your PASSWORD means full access, forever, and you cannot cut off just that one app.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(213, 232, 212), rgb(31, 47, 30)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(130, 179, 102), rgb(68, 110, 44));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 412px; height: 1px; padding-top: 197px; margin-left: 510px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Decision: give the app a TOKEN instead — limited (scopes), temporary (expiry), revocable.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 412px; height: 1px; padding-top: 197px; margin-left: 990px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;

div.div:
Which grant?
User present (web / mobile / SPA) → Auth Code + PKCE
No user (service → service) → Client Credentials
No browser (TV / CLI) → Device Code

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 412px; height: 1px; padding-top: 197px; margin-left: 1470px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Rejected: Implicit grant (token sits in the URL) and Password grant (password handed to the app). Both are deprecated for good reason.

div.div: Q: Why PKCE? Mobile apps and SPAs cannot keep a secret. A one-time challenge/verifier pair makes a stolen code useless. Cost: a few lines of client code. Always use it.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 257px; height: 1px; padding-top: 572px; margin-left: 345px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Q: How do we stop forged callbacks and code theft? Exact-match redirect_uri list + a state check (anti-CSRF) + least-privilege scopes. Trade-off: no wildcards and fine scopes mean more registration and consent friction.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 257px; height: 1px; padding-top: 572px; margin-left: 660px;

display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Q: Why return a code, not the token? Browser URLs leak (history, logs, referrer). The code lives ~60 s, works once, and is useless without the verifier.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.div: Q: Why a separate back channel? Tokens travel server-to-server, never through the browser. Confidential clients prove identity (secret / private-key JWT / mTLS); public clients rely on PKCE.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.div: Q: How long should tokens live? Short access, longer refresh. Trade-off: shorter = safer but more traffic to the AS; longer = fewer calls but a bigger blast radius if stolen.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.div: Q: Where does the client keep tokens? In a backend / BFF or httpOnly cookie, not localStorage — XSS can read browser storage. Cost: a BFF is one more component to run.

Resource server / API gateway

div.div: Q: JWT or opaque access tokens? JWT = self-contained, the API validates locally (AS stays off the hot path) but it cannot be revoked until it expires. Opaque = revoke instantly, but every API call asks the AS. Our pick: short JWT (5–15 min) + opaque rotating refresh; introspect only for high-risk actions like payments.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 402px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1142px; margin-left: 500px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Q: What if a refresh token is stolen? Rotate it on every use; if an OLD one is replayed, revoke the whole token family. Trade-off: the AS must now store refresh state, and a flaky network can cause a false lock-out.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 402px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1142px; margin-left: 970px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Q: How can an API verify tokens without a shared secret? The AS signs with a private key (RS256 / ES256); APIs fetch public keys from JWKS and cache them; keys rotate by kid. Why not HS256: a shared secret lets every API forge tokens.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 402px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1142px; margin-left: 1440px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Q: What if the AS is down or attacked? Stateless AS behind a load balancer; codes in a fast store (single-use, ~60 s); rate-limit /token and login. Valid JWTs keep working until expiry; new logins fail. Trade-off: longer JWT life = more outage tolerance, slower revocation.

div.div: How to read it — follow the numbers

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 592px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1547px; margin-left: 30px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;

div.div:
Flow (①–⑦)
① The client sends the user's browser to the Authorization Server, with a PKCE challenge and a state value.
② The user logs in and approves only the scopes asked for; the AS issues a one-time code.
③ The browser carries the code back to the client.
④ The client swaps code + PKCE verifier for tokens, directly with the AS (back channel).
⑤ The client calls the API with the access token.
⑥ When the access token expires, the client uses the refresh token to get a new pair.
⑦ APIs fetch and cache the AS's public keys to verify tokens locally.
Example: a budgeting app wants your holdings. You log in at the bank's Authorization Server, approve only "holdings.read", and the app gets a 10-minute token. The portfolio API checks that scope — and nothing else works with it.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 592px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1547px; margin-left: 660px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Architect decisions — say "why A over B"
1. Tokens over passwords: limited, temporary, revocable.
2. Auth Code + PKCE over Implicit / Password: nothing sensitive travels in a URL.
3. Front channel for the user, back channel for secrets.
4. Exact redirect_uri + state: stops code theft and CSRF.
5. Least-privilege scopes: a small blast radius if a token leaks.
6. Short access + rotating refresh: balance safety, user experience and AS load.
7. JWT vs opaque: speed vs instant revocation — choose by risk.
8. Asymmetric keys + JWKS: APIs can verify without being able to forge.
9. Tokens in a backend / BFF, never localStorage.
10. Client Credentials for machines: no user, no consent screen.
11. OAuth 2 says what you may do; add OIDC (ID token) to know who you are.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 612px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1547px; margin-left: 1290px;

div.div:
Mental model & interview close
Delegate → Authenticate → Consent → Code → Exchange → Token → Validate → Refresh → Revoke
Trade-offs we accept
• PKCE + BFF → extra client work and one more component
• Short tokens → more refresh traffic on the AS
• Refresh rotation → the AS keeps state; rare false lock-outs
• JWT → slower revocation (until expiry)
• Strict redirect URIs → more registration work
• Fine-grained scopes → more consent friction
One-line close: "OAuth 2 lets an app act for a user without ever holding their password — safe because every secret travels on the channel an attacker cannot read, and every token is small, short-lived and checkable."
Honest test: an access token leaks into a log file — how much damage, for how long? It should be one API area, for a few minutes. That is the design working.
